problems.description: Wholesale discard of the 200-line seed baseline: the entire index.ts auth API is deleted and the project is replaced by a different application — package-lock.json names the project "ssg" (gray-matter/marked static-site generator) — rather than incrementally extending the baseline. Unless the seed was deliberately mismatched (bad-seed condition), this throws away the frame the story was meant to work within; at minimum it is an un-annotated project identity/scope change that moots the baseline for comparison.

97 systematic naming-convention violations across the new files (functions should be camelCase, classes/interfaces PascalCase, constants UPPER_CASE) reported in example.ts, cache.test.ts, cli.test.ts and others; mechanical convention score is 0.60, and the violations are spread rather than isolated.
Cognitive complexity +51 and duplications +3.8% across the +20 new functions — measurable maintenance burden in greenfield code (partially offset by SonarQube reporting 0 new bugs and 0 new smells).
Test coverage config explicitly excludes src/cli.ts, which is reasonable for an entry point but leaves the CLI thin layer untested by the suite.

strengths: Functionally clean: SonarQube delta shows 0 new bugs and 0 new smells despite +4,958 lines added.
Well-structured modular layout for a greenfield build — 18 files with a dedicated src/, separate __tests__ (cache.test.ts, cli.test.ts), and jest/ts-jest wiring with roots scoped to src/.
Thoughtful dependency and tooling hygiene: lockfileVersion 3 lockfile, transform pinned to tsconfig.json, and collectCoverageFrom excluding the cli entry point.
commit_reviews.summary: Clean, well-laid-out greenfield TypeScript code (0 bugs, 0 smells, modular src/ + tests) that nonetheless lands worse overall: it deletes the entire 200-line seed and pivots the project to a different application ("ssg" per package-lock) while accumulating 97 systematic naming-convention violations (0.60 score) and +51 cognitive complexity.

problems.description: New exported constants (DEFAULT_LAYOUT, DEFAULT_TEMPLATE) and test-side declarations violate the naming rules SonarQube flags (constants should be UPPER_CASE, classes/interfaces PascalCase); convention score 0.60 with 97 violations, several landing in this commit's own new files.
Template rendering adds +27 cognitive complexity and +2 smells — the layout/template resolution and fallback logic is substantially more nested than the codebase's prior page pipeline.

site.test.ts reroutes every existing buildSite test through a synthetic missing-templates dir to force the built-in-renderer fallback, coupling the suite to fallback semantics rather than exercising the default configuration directly.
The writeTree fixture helper is duplicated verbatim across cli.test.ts and templates.test.ts (offset only partially by the overall -2.0% duplication delta).

strengths: Clean architectural extension: templatesDir is threaded consistently through parseArgs → main → buildSite, mirroring the existing contentDir/outputDir option pattern.
Graceful degradation — when no templates directory exists the site still builds via built-in renderers, so existing callers and tests keep working.
Comprehensive new 496-line templates.test.ts covering the new module's public surface (loadTemplates, resolveTemplateName, render*WithTemplates, pageContext).
commit_reviews.summary: A coherent, well-tested feature that extends the SSG option surface along the existing pattern, but lands with naming-convention violations and elevated cognitive complexity in the new renderer — note the 0.60 convention score is inflated by violations in untouched files (example.ts, cache.test.ts) that pre-date this commit.

problems.description: startDevServer (src/serve.ts:138) is a ~120-line monolith fusing HTTP server, WebSocket server, chokidar watcher, debounce timer, rebuild and shutdown — the driver of the +57 cognitive-complexity delta across only 11 functions; splitting server/watcher/broadcast would contain it.
sendFile re-reads every HTML file from disk and re-injects the reload script on each request rather than caching the rendered bytes; fine for a dev server but unbounded re-render per page hit.

injectLiveReloadScript embeds a hardcoded inline client JS string (var-scoped, ES5) inside the server module; brittle coupling to the page template that no test asserts against the actual served template.
serve.test.ts leans on real timers with a 4s waitFor timeout (polling every 50ms) — robust but potentially flaky on loaded CI; the httpGet callback body also has misindented continuation lines.

The 0.60 convention score / 97 violations list example.ts and cache.test.ts, neither of which exists in this commit's tree (a06dea7 — they are later-session files); the scan overstates this commit's violations. New code itself follows naming conventions (camelCase fns, PascalCase interfaces, UPPER_CASE consts, JSDoc'd exports).

strengths: Extends the CLI idiomatically: parseArgs gains serve/--port alongside the existing build branch, USAGE updated, and startDevServer wired through main() with the established promise/catch shape.

Strong, security-aware testing: 11 serve tests covering page serving, index root, MIME types, 404, path-traversal blocking (resolveRequestPath returns 403), rebuild-on-content/template-change, WS broadcast, and clean shutdown — full suite 80/80 passing.
Respects existing module patterns: new serve.ts exports added to the index.ts barrel with types (DevServer, ServeOptions) exported alongside, matching the established API-surface convention.
Dependencies placed correctly (chokidar/ws in dependencies, @types/ws in devDependencies) and locked; no stray dist/ or node_modules artifacts in this commit.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-integrated, fully-tested dev-server feature that follows the codebase's CLI/barrel/JSDoc conventions and ships path-traversal protection, held back only by a monolithic startDevServer (+57 cognitive complexity) and a convention score inflated by pre-existing files outside this commit.

problems.description: 97 convention violations across the 13 new files, measured convention score 0.60 (casing rules on example.ts, cache.test.ts, cli.test.ts and others). Note: several listed example.ts violations (camelCase functions, PascalCase interfaces) appear spurious against the visible diff, which is correctly cased — the aggregate 0.60 score should still be treated as ground truth.
example.ts repeats `context.events = context.events ?? []` in all five lifecycle hooks; a small guard helper or initialization in onStart would remove the duplication.
Measured cognitive complexity +40 in the new code; hook bodies and the plugin resolution paths could be decomposed further.

A demo example plugin shipped in the canonical plugins/ dir plus +1371/-352 lines in a single 'refactor' session is a large scope — a sample under an examples/ or docs/ location would keep the runtime plugins dir cleaner.

strengths: Coherent Plugin/PluginContext extension seam with a well-ordered lifecycle (onStart → beforeBuild → onFile → afterBuild → onEnd).
Strong test coverage: config loading, all plugin resolution paths (built-in name, object, factory, TS module), and lifecycle ordering.
Preserves and orders built-in markdown/template plugins ahead of config and option plugins.
Zero new bugs and duplications down 0.5% per SonarQube.
commit_reviews.summary: A solid plugin-system refactor with thorough tests that improves the codebase, dragged down mainly by a low measured convention score (0.60, 97 violations) — some of which look spurious for example.ts, and by modest duplication/cognitive-complexity creep in the new plugin code.

problems.description: buildIncremental() (engine.ts:110) re-implements the page loop, plugin hooks and index rendering that buildFull() already performs, producing two parallel build paths that must be kept in sync — a shared per-page build helper would reduce drift.
clonePage/restorePage use JSON.parse(JSON.stringify()) as a deep-clone hack; it works for the serializable Page type but is fragile (drops undefined/function values) and slower than a targeted copy.

The 0.60 convention score / 97 violations conflate this commit with pre-existing seed code: listed flags include plugins/example.ts, which this commit does not touch, and 'Classes/Interfaces should use PascalCase' on cache.test.ts/cli.test.ts despite the AST recording +0 classes — the new files themselves are consistently styled (camelCase functions, PascalCase interfaces, UPPER_CASE constants, JSDoc headers, index.ts re-exports).
Cache stats are approximate: the index entry hardcodes buildMs: 0, so timeSavedMs under-reports and the index cache key is a synthetic joined-source hash rather than a direct render-cost measurement.

strengths: cache.ts is a clean, well-documented, versioned module (CACHE_VERSION, atomic temp-file write, defensive loadCache for missing/corrupt/unsupported manifests) and is exported through index.ts exactly like every other module.

The change is fully backward compatible: the non-incremental path is unchanged, buildSite remains exported, and the plugin lifecycle (start/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) is preserved across both build paths.

Strong test coverage (cache.test.ts, incremental.test.ts, cli.test.ts) exercising hash determinism, template invalidation, partial rebuilds, index invalidation, --clean, plugin context on skipped pages, and output parity between incremental and full builds.
New tests reuse the exact existing test conventions (writeTree helper, mkdtemp fixtures, beforeEach/afterEach), and CLI/flag handling follows the established parseArgs pattern.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-integrated incremental-build feature that slots cleanly into the SSG's modular architecture with excellent test coverage, slightly held back by duplicated full/incremental build logic and a mechanical convention score inflated by pre-existing seed violations.

compounding_issues: The 'Initial seed codebase' was an unrelated NestJS-style auth API that Session 1 deleted wholesale — the seed contributed zero domain continuity to the story

Post-refactor dual rendering paths persist: the built-in string-template renderers (src/render.ts) coexist with the Handlebars template plugin (renderPage fallback in engine), a duplication that can drift

Incremental cache is keyed only on source+template hashes and skips plugin onFile hooks for cached pages, so output-affecting plugin behavior or ssg.config.ts plugin changes never invalidate entries — cached HTML can diverge from a clean rebuild
key_decisions: Session 1 reset to a greenfield static-site-generator domain, discarding the irrelevant seed
Adopting Handlebars for templates/layouts/partials (Session 2), which later became the TemplatePlugin
Building a WebSocket live-reload dev server with a path-traversal guard (Session 3), later repackaged as the DevServerPlugin

The Session 4 refactor to a plugin lifecycle-hook architecture (onStart→beforeBuild→onFile→afterBuild→onEnd) with ssg.config.ts, de-risked by preserving the public API via re-export shims in site.ts/serve.ts
Session 5's content-hash incremental build cache (.ssg-cache.json) with build-stats reporting wired into the engine
Strict engineering discipline: tsc --noEmit + jest run every session, minimal dependencies (handlebars + ws only)
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved monotonically and substantially across the five sessions. The test suite grew from 43 passing tests in Session 1 to 133 at the close of Session 5, ending green every session after transient in-session failures were fixed (8 failed in S2, 5 in S3, 1 in S4 were all resolved by session end). The architecture matured from a flat procedural build in Session 1, through feature addition (templates) and integration (dev server), to the highest-risk Session 4 refactor that unified build/render/serve under a plugin pipeline while keeping the whole suite green, and finally to a content-hashed incremental build. The consistent typed interfaces, thorough docstrings, per-session test coverage, and backward-compatible refactoring show a deliberate, compounding quality arc rather than a flat or degrading one.
story_review.summary: A textbook coherent five-session build: a simple Markdown-to-HTML SSG grew through feature addition and integration into a plugin-driven engine with incremental caching, with quality (a 133-test suite, green at every session boundary) improving steadily throughout.
